summary: Nicholas II, last Romanov tsar of Russia (1894-1917), clung to absolute autocracy, tolerated antisemitic pogroms, crushed the 1905 revolution with mass killings and led Russia into disastrous wars before his abdication and execution in 1918.
keywords: Protocols of the Elders of Zion

evidence.note: Crimean War defeat and Alexander II's accession in 1855 open a long segment on his reforms and murder
Nicholas born in May 1868 at the Alexander Palace near St. Petersburg
Japanese police officer slashes the future tsar with a sword during his 1891 visit to Japan
Alexander III dies in 1894 and Nicholas becomes tsar
coronation gift-bag event turns into a deadly stampede; celebrations go on regardless
royal couple fall under the sway of the French mystic healer Philippe, precursor to Rasputin
1903 Kishinev pogrom (modern Moldova) and the tsar's indifference to it
Russo-Japanese War fought over Manchuria after Port Arthur attack
troops fire on marching workers at the palace in January 1905, killing hundreds or more
tsar orders brutal suppression of the 1905 uprisings, praising executions in his diary
takes personal command of the army in WWI against his ministers' advice
1918 execution of the family by the Bolsheviks described in detail

notes: Alexander II listed as secondary because part 1 spends roughly 20 minutes on his reign, reforms and 1881 assassination; this sets covered_span start at 1855. Romanov rise in 1613 is a passing mention. Setting omits Latvia/Baltics (brief crackdown mention). occult-esoteric chosen for Philippe and Rasputin as mystic healers; quackery-pseudoscience also arguable. Brief Putin joke at the end does not count as reaching the present.
